# HamApp Windows desktop client — bounded native preview

**Built from Python standard-library Tkinter UI and Microsoft winget.** These are existing maintained platform tools; no custom installer engine or update daemon is written. The bundle is generated by the GitHub-hosted Windows runner using pinned upstream PyInstaller 6.22.3. It is an **unsigned preview**, not a validated or signed production installer.

## Architecture
- `windows_client/gui.py`: native Persian catalogue UI, search, details, explicit confirmation before operations. Never silently elevates privileges, accepts EULA, or invokes shell commands via `shell=True`.
- `windows_client/core.py`: fail-closed bounded validation and argument-array builder. Only `winget install|upgrade|show --id ID --exact --source winget` with pinned version when installing/upgrading; interactive.
- `scripts/build_windows_client_catalog.py`: validates `catalog/apps.json` against independently reviewed signer/history and `catalog/winget_packages.json` (owner-curated mapping). Only a matching current approved Windows entry and a reviewed mapping can produce an enabled button. No private data or credentials embedded.
- `run_windows_client.py`: PyInstaller/Tkinter entry point.
- `.github/workflows/windows-client-preview.yml`: hosted Windows tests + unsigned EXE build + short-lived Actions artifact. No install or execution on the owner's Windows machine.

## Safety limitations
The `catalog/winget_packages.json` mapping intentionally remains empty. All entries are planned, so **install/upgrade/show actions are disabled**. Never silently add a package mapping from a downloaded manifest, GitHub PR or untrusted installer. Confirm that the pinned winget package ID/version corresponds to the previously approved signed release via an independent publisher/channel. GitHub history metadata is review-only, not cryptographic proof of the actual winget source binary.

The Windows Package Manager honors Windows/UAC and package license prompts. Do not use `--silent`, `--accept-package-agreements`, `--ignore-security-hash`, `--force`, custom overrides or source override. Distributing an unsigned EXE may trigger Windows SmartScreen; do not instruct bypassing device security policies. The preview artifact expires after three days, is not placed on the public site and has not undergone real-device installer QA.

## Running in development
```powershell
python scripts/build_windows_client_catalog.py
python run_windows_client.py
```

## Acceptance not yet completed
- Sign the Windows EXE with an owner-approved code signing identity outside public CI; retain certificate identity for updates.
- Review actual winget mapping / publisher ownership and confirm installed package matches approved binary provenance.
- Test real install, upgrade, downgrade rejection, UAC prompts and rollback on an approved Windows test machine.
- Verify GUI accessibility and performance on a real interactive Windows desktop session (hosted CI cannot prove GUI usability).
- Publish a tagged, signed GitHub Release only after these gates.

Microsoft official winget command documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/install
PyInstaller upstream: https://pyinstaller.org/en/latest/usage.html

## Exact WinGet installed-version readback (2026-11-02 pending CI)
- Approved WinGet install/upgrade now preflights actual registered package version via `winget export --source winget --include-versions --output <private temp JSON> --disable-interactivity`, refuses unsafe or ambiguous current versions and downgrades, then executes the requested exact interactive WinGet command.
- After WinGet exits zero, HamApp runs a **second** export, parses the official `Sources[].SourceDetails.Name == winget` and `Packages[].PackageIdentifier/Version` schema, and only reports an actual installed-version readback when the exact target version matches. Temporary system inventory is deleted; no app list is sent to GitHub.
- This is independent **WinGet package-registry readback**, not independent Authenticode installer validation, OS file-integrity attestation or real owner-device install acceptance. The public WinGet map remains empty. PR tests use a synthetic injected export; real installation cannot be accepted without owner-reviewed package identity and approval.
